title: Stack on an Array
description: Build ArrayStack on top of a plain list plus a top index. push adds x, pop removes and returns the top value, top returns it without removing, isEmpty and size report the contents. pop and top return -1 when the stack is empty.

title: Queue on an Array
description: Build ArrayQueue on a circular buffer with front and rear indices. push adds x at the back, pop removes and returns the front value, peek returns it without removing, isEmpty and size report the contents. pop and peek return -1 when the queue is empty.

title: Stack from a Queue
description: Build QueueStack using only queue operations (add to back, remove from front, size). After each push, rotate the older items behind the new one so the front of the queue is always the top of the stack. pop and top return -1 when empty.

title: Queue from Two Stacks
description: Build StackQueue with two stacks: push onto an input stack, and when the output stack is empty, pour the input stack into it so the oldest item ends up on top. pop and peek return -1 when empty.

title: Stack on a Linked List
description: Build LinkedStack where every push creates a ListNode in front of the current head, and pop unlinks the head. Keep a running size. pop and top return -1 when empty.

title: Queue on a Linked List
description: Build LinkedQueue with head and tail ListNode pointers: push appends after the tail, pop unlinks the head. Remember to clear the tail when the queue becomes empty. pop and peek return -1 when empty.

title: Balanced Brackets
description: s contains only the characters ()[]{}. Return whether every bracket is closed by the matching type in the right order. Push openers and match each closer against the top of the stack.

title: Next Greater Element
description: For each position, return the first value to its right that is strictly greater, or -1 if there is none. Walk from the right and keep a stack of candidates in decreasing order.

title: Next Greater in a Circle
description: nums is circular: after the last element comes the first. For each position return the first strictly greater value found while walking forward around the circle, or -1. Scan the array twice from the right.

title: Asteroid Collision
description: Each value is an asteroid: its size is the absolute value and its sign is its direction (positive moves right). When a right-mover meets a left-mover, the smaller one explodes; equal sizes both explode. Return the asteroids left after every collision.

title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
description: Return the sum of min(sub) over every contiguous subarray, modulo 1,000,000,007. Each value is the minimum of (left run) × (right run) subarrays; find those runs with a monotonic stack, breaking ties on one side only.
referenceCode:
def sum_subarray_mins(arr):
    mod = 1000000007
    n = len(arr)
    left = [0] * n
    right = [0] * n
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and arr[stack[-1]] > arr[i]:
            stack.pop()
        left[i] = i - stack[-1] if stack else i + 1
        stack.append(i)
    stack = []
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        while stack and arr[stack[-1]] >= arr[i]:
            stack.pop()
        right[i] = stack[-1] - i if stack else n - i
        stack.append(i)
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        total = (total + arr[i] * left[i] * right[i]) % mod
    return total

title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
description: The range of a subarray is its largest value minus its smallest. Return the sum of ranges over every contiguous subarray. That equals (sum of subarray maximums) − (sum of subarray minimums).
referenceCode:
def sub_array_ranges(nums):
    def contribution(values, better):
        n = len(values)
        total = 0
        stack = []
        for i in range(n + 1):
            while stack and (i == n or better(values[i], values[stack[-1]])):
                mid = stack.pop()
                left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
                total += values[mid] * (mid - left) * (i - mid)
            stack.append(i)
        return total

    maxima = contribution(nums, lambda a, b: a >= b)
    minima = contribution(nums, lambda a, b: a <= b)
    return maxima - minima

title: Remove K Digits
description: num is a non-negative integer written as a string. Remove exactly k digits so the remaining number is as small as possible. Return it without leading zeros, or "0" if nothing is left.
constraints: num has no leading zeros except the number 0 itself.

title: Min Stack
description: Build MinStack with push, pop, top and getMin, all in O(1). Store each value together with the minimum at that depth. Calls to pop, top and getMin are only made on a non-empty stack.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: A window of size k slides from left to right across nums. Return the maximum of each window. Keep a deque of indices whose values decrease from front to back.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: heights describes an elevation map made of bars of width 1. Return how much water it holds after rain. Move two pointers inward, always from the side with the lower wall, tracking the highest wall seen on each side.

title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
description: heights are bars of width 1. Return the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram. When a shorter bar arrives, pop taller bars and measure how far each could stretch.
referenceCode:
def largest_rectangle_area(heights):
    stack = []
    best = 0
    n = len(heights)
    for i in range(n + 1):
        current = heights[i] if i < n else 0
        while stack and heights[stack[-1]] >= current:
            height = heights[stack.pop()]
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            best = max(best, height * (i - left - 1))
        stack.append(i)
    return best

title: Largest Rectangle of Ones
description: grid holds 0s and 1s. Return the area of the largest rectangle containing only 1s. Treat each row as the base of a histogram of stacked ones and reuse the largest-rectangle-in-histogram idea.

title: Stock Span
description: StockSpanner.next(price) receives one daily price at a time. It returns the span: how many consecutive days, ending today, had a price less than or equal to today's. Keep a stack of (price, span) pairs.

title: Find the Celebrity
description: knows[i][j] is 1 when person i knows person j. A celebrity is known by everyone else and knows no one. Return the celebrity's index, or -1. Eliminate one candidate per comparison, then confirm the survivor.

title: LRU Cache
description: Build LRUCache(capacity). get(key) returns the stored value or -1. put(key, value) inserts or updates, and when the cache is over capacity it evicts the least recently used key. Both run in O(1): pair a hash map with a doubly linked list ordered by recency.
referenceCode:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, key=0, value=0):
        self.key = key
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.nodes = {}
        self.head = Node()
        self.tail = Node()
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self.head

    def _unlink(self, node):
        node.prev.next = node.next
        node.next.prev = node.prev

    def _push_front(self, node):
        node.next = self.head.next
        node.prev = self.head
        self.head.next.prev = node
        self.head.next = node

    def get(self, key):
        node = self.nodes.get(key)
        if node is None:
            return -1
        self._unlink(node)
        self._push_front(node)
        return node.value

    def put(self, key, value):
        node = self.nodes.get(key)
        if node is not None:
            node.value = value
            self._unlink(node)
            self._push_front(node)
            return
        if len(self.nodes) == self.capacity:
            oldest = self.tail.prev
            self._unlink(oldest)
            del self.nodes[oldest.key]
        node = Node(key, value)
        self.nodes[key] = node
        self._push_front(node)

title: LFU Cache
description: Build LFUCache(capacity). get(key) returns the value or -1 and counts as a use. put(key, value) inserts or updates (also a use). When full, evict the key with the fewest uses; among ties, evict the least recently used. Keep a map from use count to an ordered group of keys, plus the current minimum count.
